fields.v: Arman, M. S., Molybog, I. (2026). Compact Documentation for Coding Agents: A Benchmark, an Optimizer, and Why It Does Not Transfer. arXiv:2609.31587v1 [cs.SE], 25 Sep 2026
Preprint — arXiv; marked 'Preprint' on p. 1, no venue in the arXiv metadata (comment '13 pages. Code and data: https://github.com/haw-ai-i/roundtrip')
Daffodil International University, Dhaka, Bangladesh (Arman); HawAII, University of Hawai'i at Manoa, USA (Molybog)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Proposes an approach — roundtrip benchmark scoring descriptions by whether code regenerated from them passes the original tests; benchmark-driven optimizer of the describe prompt; also evaluates whether such documentation helps issue resolution (negative result)
fields.why: Judgement: contributions (1)-(2) are the benchmark and the describe-prompt optimizer, but the paper calls the downstream test 'the question that motivated the work' (p. 1, 6), so 'Evaluates' as main or secondary nature is also defensible; Q13 applies either way because an approach (the optimized describe prompt) is proposed
fields.doubt: O artigo propõe o benchmark e o otimizador, mas a pergunta que o motivou é se a documentação ajuda a resolver issues (p. 1, 6). Decide se a natureza principal é Proposes an evaluation method ou Evaluates.

fields.v: (A) Optimized describe prompt: natural-language 'specification' of a source file written by an LLM, prompt discovered by a hill-climbing loop scored on the roundtrip benchmark (no product name or version); variants: full-length optimized description and ~80-word compact description. (B) Baseline hand-written describe prompt. (C) OpenWiki (LangChain 2026), external documentation tool for coding agents, version not stated. (D) SWE-ContextBench retrieved past-task context

Per-file natural-language description/specification: module preamble (all imports, constants with exact literal values), each class/function incl. private members with exact signature, defaults, attributes, logic, return paths and exception conditions (discovered prompt, App. D/E); contract file naming public symbols for regeneration

Benchmark: describe (source -> description, tests excluded) -> regenerate (separate model, description + empty scaffold + contract file only) -> evaluate (original tests). Optimizer: proposer rewrites describe prompt -> benchmark score -> keep if objective J (mean fidelity - 0.1 x words/300) improves. Downstream: description of pre-fix file added to issue prompt
None in the flow (automatic loop); hand-written descriptions only for the three constructed boundary codebases
Single artefact (one file-level description supplied to the agent; full describe-regenerate-evaluate pipeline run for the benchmark)

Not classified by the authors; they treat 'a description as durable software source' from which code is regenerated (closest to spec-as-source, reviewer's reading); downstream use is documentation added to context
fields.why: Authors do not classify; 'treats a description as durable software source' (p. 9) supports a spec-as-source reading for the roundtrip benchmark, but the downstream use is a description added to the agent's context next to the code; Not classifiable is also defensible
fields.doubt: Os autores não classificam. A frase 'description as durable software source' (p. 9) sugere spec-as-source, mas no uso real a descrição é só contexto extra junto ao código. Escolhe spec-as-source ou not classifiable.

fields.v: Existing code bases: SWE-bench Verified single-file fixtures (regeneration, issue resolution with source withheld or present), SWE-ContextBench Lite issues; plus three hand-built small codebases (add a method honouring a contract)

11 roundtrip fixtures (48-2,470 lines, mean 946 +/- 760) from 429 of 2,294 Verified instances passing the filter; 3 hand-built codebases; Kind-B multi-file set 50 fixtures (43 paired); django Kind-B 15; SWE-ContextBench Lite 99 tasks, 12 repos (58 paired in head-to-head)

Open-source Python: sympy (roundtrip fixtures), django, matplotlib, scikit-learn, requests, astropy, seaborn, xarray, sphinx, flask (SWE-ContextBench); access-control policy engine and configuration examples (hand-built)
N/A (no human participants)

Description density (description tokens / code tokens); description length in words (penalty in objective); prompt tokens qualitatively in Sec. 7.3 (description costs more prompt tokens than it saves). No money or time

Roundtrip fidelity (fraction of original tests passed by regenerated code); fraction of tests passed (source withheld); tasks resolved (all fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass tests pass); pass counts on boundary tasks
Not measured
Not measured
Failure modes of regeneration (lost output literal, lost imports, lost constraint, recitation blocked); verbatim recitation monitoring (contamination); edit attrition (no scorable edit)
Automatic: unit tests / official SWE-bench and SWE-ContextBench Docker harnesses; token counts with one subword tokenizer; failure modes by hand analysis

Agent harness not named for any configuration (models only; local Qwen agent unnamed). Metrics: original / official tests (fidelity = fraction of tests passed by regenerated code; resolved = all FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS pass; boundary tasks = attempts or facts passed). No run cost (tokens, money, time) reported except qualitatively in Sec. 7.3; density = description tokens / code tokens. No success criterion for a configuration is stated by the authors.

- Boundary tasks, Flash-lite + description (hand-written for the 3 codebases; Pro-written otherwise): contract only in description 3/3 on each codebase; contract visible 3/3; facts 1/5, 3/5, 5/5 by completeness; compact 38w and verbose 664w both 5/5. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured

Harder 28-key task, Flash-lite / Gemini 2.5 Flash / Gemma 3 4B (Table 10): compact and fair (buried) verbose 8/8, 4/4, 8/8; verbose without exact keys 0/8, 0/4, 0/8. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured

- OpenWiki documentation + same Gemini family regenerate (Table 5): fidelity saferepr 0.00, contains 0.67, unitsystem 0.00; deny-override task, Flash-lite, 0/4 (Table 6). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured

Kind-B django, Gemini 3.1 Pro: issue 9/15, + compact 8/15, + full 4/15. SCB django control, Gemini 3.1 Pro: issue 14/29, + retrieved context 15/29. SCB django, Gemini 3.1 Pro: issue 15/32, + compact 16/32. SCB Lite, Gemini 3.8 Flash: issue 33/58, + compact 29/58, + context 30/58 (McNemar p = 0.22 and 0.25 vs issue); full issue-only run 37/68 scored (Table 11). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors (each condition); cost: not measured

Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: no criterion stated by the authors
fields.why: Round 2 rebuilt the verdicts on its own cut-off ('quality partly when it resolves part but not nearly all tasks', admitted in its 'why') and gave 'works'/'does not work' on cost from qualitative token remarks. The paper states no success criterion for any configuration (tests define per-task pass, not a configuration threshold), so per the 2026-11-23 rule every verdict is 'no criterion stated by the authors'. Values re-checked against Tables 2-3, 5-10 and pp. 3-8, 10-11 and kept

fields.v: Several experiments: (1) boundary tasks on 3 hand-built codebases and a fact-lookup task; (2) roundtrip benchmark on 11 Verified fixtures; (3) OpenWiki vs own descriptions on 3 fixtures; (4) optimizer with 3 training / 2 held-out fixtures; (5) issue resolution source withheld (11 fixtures) and source present (5 settings, 3 models); (6) editing without loading the file (single files, 33 runs). Baselines: no description / issue only; base describe prompt; OpenWiki. Held constant: model within each comparison, temperature 0 for generation, same regenerate/evaluate stages, descriptions from pre-fix file, official Docker harness; paired tasks only (tasks with scorable edit under every condition). Acceptance: original/oracle unit tests, fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass. Repetitions: 3 runs per fixture (benchmark, source withheld), 3-8 attempts on boundary tasks; not stated for the source-present runs (Kind-B, SWE-ContextBench). Human intervention: none

Completeness, not length, drives fidelity (Pearson density-fidelity 0.88). Own descriptions beat OpenWiki on all 3 fixtures (0.73/1.00/0.85 vs 0.00/0.67/0.00). Optimizer raises held-out fidelity 0.5 -> 1.0. Source withheld: optimized 0.71 vs baseline 0.21 vs issue 0.08. Source present: no documentation condition improves on issue-only by more than one task; full description worst wherever run (django 4/15 vs 9/15); SCB Lite issue 33 vs compact 29 (p = 0.22) vs context 30 (p = 0.25), not significant; sign test on Kind-B dominated by ties

Benchmark separated descriptions (fixtures from 0 to 1 fidelity; not saturated). Positive control on SCB django (retrieved context 15 vs 14) presented as showing the harness can detect an effect, though a one-task difference. Limitations stated: small fixture set (11 + 3) from one language and project family; largest downstream run one economical model and one summary length (~80 words); stronger-model replications only on django; attrition not perfectly random (documentation conditions no-edit more often); benchmark needs a capable regenerator (two open-weight models scored zero); optimizer proof of concept (few fixtures, iterations, one proposer); contamination controls incomplete

Documentation of this kind pays only when the source cannot be loaded (compression format for code that does not fit context); redundant, occasionally harmful (invites rewriting), when source is present. Next step: establish the boundary at repository scale where whole codebases do not fit. Limitations as in 'did the method work'

Code and data: https://github.com/haw-ai-i/roundtrip (code, task list, generated descriptions, per-task results released). Prompts verbatim in App. D-E (discovered prompt text partly interleaved by pdftotext). Optimizer results only in Fig. 3. Positive control is a single-task difference (15 vs 14), which the paper itself says a paired test cannot distinguish for the compact case. Model names as printed (gemini3.5-flash, gemini-2.5-pro, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Qwen 3.6, Flash-lite). No pre-registration stated. Language: Python. Funding: NSF NRT-AI, ACCESS, NPC Labs compute
